findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: The handwashing sink where meats and cheeses are sliced lacked soap and paper towels. Discussed with the PIC and soap and paper towels were provided to the hand sink to correct the violation. Ensure that all hand sinks are equipped with hand soap, paper towels, and running warm water.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.11 Handwashing Cleanser, Availability. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.comment: An unknown liquid food was observed actively producing bubbles, as the food was stored inside of the walk in cooler. The liquid food item appeared to be spoiled and not in safe condition to consume. The item also lacked date marking and an identification label. The liquid was pulled from the shelf to be discarded. Violation corrected. Ensure that Time/Temperature control (TCS) foods are date marked and are in good condition for consumption.
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Safe, Unadulterated, and Honestly Presented. FOOD shall be safe, unADULTERATED, and, as specified under § 3-601.12, honestly presented.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: Despite the service line being in operation, there wasn’t a sanitizer solution available. Discussed with PIC and a solution was created and tested at 300ppm (quat) to correct the violation. Ensure that sani solutions are always available if preparing, handling, or serving food.
findings.citation_text: 4-303.11(B) Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability. (B) Except for those that are generated on-site at the time of use, chemical SANITIZERS that are used to sanitize EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-7, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment: The baffles of the hood suppression system above the fryers were a bit accumulated with dried grease. The PIC mentioned that the facility manual cleans the baffles, however, the system will need to be serviced by a professional to clean the internal work. Be sure to hire a professional hood service company to maintain duct work.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following sinks are in need of repair:
- the current caulk on both triple sinks in the deli area are starting to pull from the wall 
- the current caulk on the triple sink in the meat/seafood area is starting to pull from the wall
Ensure that sinks are cleaned and recaulked to prevent debris accumulation and assure smooth and easily cleanable surfaces.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Overall, the facility is in need of MAJOR CLEANING in the deli area. Floors, walls, ceilings, and sides of cooking equipment throughout the back of the house deli area contained heavy amounts of food debris and grease debris. The areas were shown to the PIC. Be sure that areas are cleaned and maintained clean as frequent as necessary.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.12 Cleaning, Frequency and Restrictions. (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer dispenser in the meat/seafood area appears to not be functioning properly. The sanitizer bucket, as well as the triple sink tested at 0ppm (quat). After changing the chemical’s bag, the solution remained at 0ppm (quat). The facility will utilize the butcher shop’s triple to sink to access sanitizer until the sink can be repaired. Ensure that the sanitizer solution tests at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: There were at least 20 boxes observed on the floor of the shared walk in freezer. The boxes were pilled on top of each other and have started to fall onto the floor. An employee started to rearrange the freezer during the inspection to correct the violation. Ensure that food is stored in a manner that prevents contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used.
findings.comment: The shared walk in freezer is lacking proper lighting. There was minimal visibility without using flashlights. A light bulb was provided to correct the violation.Ensure that better lighting is provided to the unit.
findings.citation_text: 6-303.11(A) Intensity. The light intensity shall be: (A) At least 108 lux (10 foot candles) at a distance of 75 cm (30 inches) above the floor, in walk-in refrigeration units and dry FOOD storage areas and in other areas and rooms during periods of cleaning;

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices.
findings.comment: The faucet of the triple sink in the butcher room was observed with a few leaks. There was water leaking from the faucet into the basin of the sink. Discussed with PIC. Ensure that sink faucets are maintained in good repair and never in leaking condition.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.15(B) System Maintained in Good Repair. A plumbing system shall be: (B) Maintained in good repair.

findings.comment: There was a significant amount of ice buildup on the floor of the walk in freezer in the butcher shop. Ice buildup was observed on the floor underneath the storage shelf(to the right of the door). Discussed with PIC. Ensure that cleaning of walk in units occur as often as necessary to prevent ice buildup.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket along the hot line was tested at 0ppm (q). A sani bucket was recreated and tested at 200ppm (q). Ensure that all sanitizer buckets are maintained at the manufacturer’s recommended concentration in order to properly sanitize food contact surfaces and utensils.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
Observed a box of raw bacon stored above a box of jalapeño peppers in the meat department’s walk-in cooler. Discussed with PIC that raw meats should be stored beneath any ready-to-eat food item. The box of bacon was removed from the above shelf. Ensure that raw meats are always stored beneath RTE food items to prevent cross-contamination. 

3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
Observed several meat products to exceed the manufacturer’s use-by-date stored in the floor coolers. These items include but aren't limited to sliced deli meats, pork bacon, pork sausage, and ground sausage. The use-by-dates ranged from 4/28/2024 - 5/30/2024. Most of the meat items (bacon, pork sausage & deli meats) were manufactured, however, the other items (ground sausage) were processed on site. PIC mentioned that he has no knowledge of any written procedures on training employees to follow the “first in-first out” method and that employees are vocally trained to follow FIFO. The expired meat products were pulled from the coolers. The inspector suggested the PIC to have an employee thoroughly go through the cooler to check on use-by-dates. 

In the future, conduct a daily check on use-by-dates to ensure freshness of product. 


3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed that vent covers of the walk in cooler (deli department) to be heavily soiled with debris. Discussed with PIC. PIC mentioned that an employee would clean the covers very soon. Ensure that the vent covers of the walk in cooler are cleaned frequently to prevent soil accumulation. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.
